```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The payer is stronger in A. A platform or engineering lead with CI tooling budget, at a $20-50/developer/month anchor (Harness add-on), means one small team could produce meaningful revenue within 90 days. B depends on financially strained individual consumers at $8-24/month.",
    "A has a cheaper, better-fitting acquisition channel. GitHub Marketplace listing is free and self-serve. B's own sourced benchmarks put Google Career & Employment cost-per-lead at $62-118 against a sub-$25/month price, and B concedes that payback depends on an unverified conversion rate.",
    "B has structural problems the brief itself admits: the need is largely one-time and ends at re-employment, which caps lifetime value; at least four free or freemium direct competitors are live; and gaps caused by health, caregiving, or disability carry real harm and reputational risk under light AI supervision.",
    "A's main risk is that teams will not trust an AI tool to gate tests, and the cold start with no test history makes that harder. Shipping the tool as an advisory signal can partly sidestep this. A's demand evidence also includes a user valuing impact-sorting and auto-ticketing, which suggests advisory value exists without gating.",
    "Both ideas sit in crowded spaces. A's competition includes enterprise-priced incumbents (Develocity, which only lists contact-sales pricing) alongside unmonetized open-source clones, which leaves a plausible self-serve middle-price wedge. B's competitors already include free, functioning tools at the low end where B would sit."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's willingness-to-pay demand quote from every.to ('I don't have $100–$150 per hour to spend on a career coach... but I do have a subscription to ChatGPT') shows the user substituting a general ChatGPT subscription for coaching, not paying for a dedicated gap-reframing tool. It arguably undercuts B's case, and the other demand quotes show anxiety but no evidence of payment. B's six-week solo build claim is also not marked unsourced but has no source, and one competitor's pricing (CoachGPT) is NOT FOUND.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Both briefs describe crowded markets with thin differentiation. A's demand evidence is also weak: one quote comes from an employee of a flaky-test vendor (Trunk), the price anchor is a broader Harness add-on rather than a like-for-like product, and A's six-week MVP is explicitly unsourced. A wins mainly on B2B payer economics and a cheaper channel, not on stronger proof of demand."
}
```
